quotes.text: The problem isn't that people don't want to automate. It's that connecting different systems is hard. Each system has its own way of handling authentication, its own data format, its own rules.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the real barrier to automation that integration platforms solve.

quotes.text: Think of Power Automate as a bicycle. Great for getting around the office. Logic Apps is a delivery truck. Built for heavier loads and longer routes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A vivid analogy that distinguishes the two Microsoft automation tools.

quotes.text: The connectors handle the plumbing, the workflows handle the logic, and the agents handle the decisions that used to require a human in the loop
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the layered model of agentic automation in one sentence.

quotes.text: For most people starting out, the answer is simple. Start with consumption. It costs virtually nothing to try.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, low-risk recommendation for choosing a Logic Apps pricing model.

quotes.text: You don't have to be a developer to build automations and you don't have to be an IT pro to run them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the episode's message that Logic Apps lowers the barrier to automation.

takeaways: Azure Logic Apps is a serverless workflow service that connects systems like SharePoint, Teams, Outlook, SQL and Salesforce through triggers, actions and more than 1,400 connectors.
Start with the Consumption plan for low or spiky workloads and move to Standard only when high volumes make its fixed monthly price cheaper or you need dedicated compute and network control.
Logic Apps is evolving into an orchestration layer for AI, where natural-language workflow creation and AI agents handle exceptions that rigid workflows could not.
hook: Copying information between SharePoint, Teams, email and databases by hand is slow and error-prone, and custom integration code takes weeks. This episode explains Azure Logic Apps in plain English for IT pros, business analysts and Microsoft admins, covering triggers, connectors, pricing models, real examples and the shift to agentic automation.
